title: SEBI Clarifies Rules for Private Share Transfers in Unlisted Companies
summary: Prevents illegal public offerings disguised as private secondary share sales.

blocks.title: 📰 2. 🏛️ REGULATORY BODIES NEWS
blocks.text: 🪝 SEBI Clarifies Rules for Private Share Transfers in Unlisted Companies. Key development for Banking & General Awareness.

items: Prevents illegal public offerings disguised as private secondary share sales.
Secondary transfer of unlisted company shares by an existing shareholder to **≤200 buyers in a FY** is **NOT** treated as a public issue.
Contractual rights like **Right of First Refusal (ROFR)** can be honored.
Exceeding **200 buyers per FY** automatically converts the transaction into a **Deemed Public Issue**.
200 buyers limit per FY for secondary unlisted share deals vs 200 private placement limit under Sec 42 Companies Act 2013.
🎯 Exam Angle → Focus on statutory circular guidelines, compliance deadlines, penal provisions, and applicability thresholds across scheduled banks.
